name: Acceptance suite-3 test 62 - a single leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped, then the policy validates
note: docs/acceptance-suite-3.md Campaign A. Documented preprocessing: exactly ONE leading UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) is stripped, then the policy parses normally. A second leading BOM is NOT stripped (would fail as invalid JSON), and an embedded U+FEFF inside a string is PRESERVED. Paste and file import use the same rule. policyRaw begins with a literal BOM character.
rationale: A leading UTF-8 BOM is a common artifact of Windows editors and some file exports; JSON.parse rejects it, but a single leading BOM carries no semantic content, so stripping exactly one and then parsing is safe and documented. Stripping more than one, or stripping embedded U+FEFF inside string values, would be data loss - so only the single leading occurrence is removed. Ref: RFC 8259 section 8.1 (implementations MAY ignore a leading BOM) + Unicode U+FEFF.
